teaser.text: Endeavour Mining is a West African gold producer: it turns ore from its mines into gold and sells the recovered metal into a global market. To understand how a dollar moves through the business, follow it from rock, to doré, to payment, and then through the costs of keeping the mines alive.

stock.title: Endeavour stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Endeavour's weighted forecast is 5,459.72 GBp by October 2027; outcomes depend on Mana and Assafou delivering durable, saleable ounces.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast is 5,459.72 GBp by October 2027, a 32% return. The investment turns on durable, saleable ounces from Mana and Assafou, not simply a higher gold price.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Endeavour's business works, who its rivals are, how management is executing, and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could Endeavour's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is 5,459.72 GBp by October 2027, a 32% return. It reaches 6,323.85 GBp by October 2029, a 57% return including dividends. The bear case carries 27% probability. The base case carries 52%; the bull case carries 21%. By October 2029, the range runs from 789.45 GBp in the bear case to 15,457.09 GBp in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Endeavour's forecast?

paragraphs.text: The base case sets EBITDA at $3,120m in October 2027. It then uses $2,796m in October 2028 and $2,990m in October 2029. The first year assumes 1.20m ounces at a $4,200 gold price, with $1,600 cash costs. That sits within the company’s production guidance and allows costs above 2025’s $1,216 per ounce. The bear case falls from $1,430m to $1,080m before ending at $1,208m, reflecting Mana’s weakness and lower gold. The bull case rises from $4,313m to $4,608m and then $5,503m, requiring stronger mine delivery and a faster Assafou ramp.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Endeavour really make?

paragraphs.text: Endeavour’s own free-cash-flow measure differs because it subtracts net investing cash flow while leaving financing payments elsewhere. Stock compensation is then deducted in “real free cash flow” as an economic cost to shareholders, even though it is not an additional cash payment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Endeavour today?

paragraphs.text: The gap between trailing and forward P/E is the first major assumption. P/E means the share price divided by earnings; the forward measure implies that forecast earnings are roughly double the recent amount. Gold can lift earnings quickly, but depletion, depreciation and impairments can pull them down.

dividend.meta_description: Endeavour’s dividend, cash coverage, plans and current yield in one concise guide.
dividend.opening: Endeavour’s minimum dividends are US$300 million for FY2026 and US$325 million for FY2027. Endeavour’s cash coverage has been uneven: payouts exceeded free cash flow by $223.5 million in 2024, while future extra returns depend on gold prices, cash generation and leverage.
dividend.closing: The full Endeavour memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Endeavour pay per share?

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to group production of 1,090–1,265 koz. Group AISC guidance is US$1,600–1,800/oz. It is based on a US$3,000 gold assumption. Mana is expected below 155 koz and above US$2,250/oz AISC. Minimum dividends are US$300 million for FY2026 and US$325 million for FY2027.

blocks.heading: Is Endeavour's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Construction created the pressure. Free cash flow means cash from operations minus cash spent on investing. It was negative $232.4 million in 2023 and recovered to $139.2 million in 2024. Payouts exceeded free cash flow by $569.0 million in 2023 and $223.5 million in 2024.

The position changed sharply in 2025. Net debt was $718.1 million in 2024. It fell to $96.8 million in 2025 as stronger cash generation supported debt repayment, although higher gold prices also helped. By July 2026, minimum dividends were set through 2028, while extra returns remained conditional on gold prices, cash generation and leverage. The next construction programme will test whether that discipline lasts.

blocks.heading: Has Endeavour kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Production landed within the upper half of guidance, continuing the company’s long record of meeting plans. Yet group delivery can hide a weak mine if another site performs unusually well. “Attributable production” means only Endeavour’s ownership share, while headline guidance generally describes 100% of mine output. Comparisons must use the same basis.

blocks.heading: What is Endeavour's revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: Revenue and operating income rose from the comparable quarter, while net income and diluted EPS fell. Production was about 283,000 ounces, down from 306,000 a year earlier, but the realised gold price was much higher. Ity improved after maintenance, while Mana lost Siou feed, Lafigué processed lower grades and Sabodala-Massawa underwent maintenance.

blocks.heading: What should Endeavour watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The company expects to report before the London market opens, followed by a webcast at 1:30 p.m. GMT. Investors should look for evidence that the planned Q4 recovery is developing through actual ore access, grades and processing, not merely through repeated guidance.

Before year-end, investors should also examine Assafou’s investment decision and first underground ore at Sabodala-Massawa. The important details are the approved scope, contracts, spending schedule and evidence that underground development is becoming a dependable source of plant feed.
